ai.description: This snake reaches 30–40 cm. It is iridescent golden-brown above with a yellow belly and a distinctive, flattened, spine-tipped tail used for anchoring in soil. It belongs to the family Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Plectrurus aureus* is best distinguished by its unique, bright yellow or golden-yellow lateral stripe that runs along the sides of its dark, iridescent body.
ai.habitat: *Plectrurus aureus* inhabits the high-altitude montane evergreen forests (sholas) and adjacent grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kerala burrowing snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its life hidden underground to navigate its subterranean habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Plectrurus aureus* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season in the Western Ghats.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Plectrurus aureus* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically inhabiting high-elevation montane forests and grasslands.
